evidence: Swap test FAIL: put a GP surgery appointment booker or a council bulky-waste collection booker into this frame and every identity-carrying element survives: plain white header with a stock line icon + name in bold body sans, pale grey-blue ground, single left column of 320px native inputs, one dark-teal rectangular primary button, bordered radio cards, label/value summary list, red-bordered 'There is a problem' error summary. Only the copy (sill gate, high water, pontoon, draught, MMSI) and the anchor glyph are bound to the harbour. With the name and copy hidden, nothing says 'tidal harbour'.

Category-guess test FAIL: predicted default for a small public-service booking flow = government-design-system look (white/near-white, one sans, dark accent button, error summary box, summary list, native controls). The render matches it element for element (root/default/1280, review/default/1280, boat/errors/1280). Predicted opposite (glossy marine-blue hero with yacht photography) is avoided, but only by falling to the default.

Similar-prompt test FAIL: brief 'online booking for a council-run campsite pitch' would produce the same anatomy, same palette, same anchor-like stock icon swap (tent), same tide-table-equivalent plain HTML table. Overlap is total on visual choices.

What is product-specific is content only: the tide times table with the sill-gate note on root, berth descriptions ('Afloat at every state of the tide', 'Settles on soft mud at low water'), the 'harbour office sends a text if the gate times change' hint. The tide table is the nearest thing to a signature but is set as an unstyled default table and is not carried into the berth or review steps where the arrival time is chosen.

unfinished: Browser-default controls: native date input showing 'yyyy/mm/dd' and native select chevrons on root (root/default/1280, 375, 320).
Identity is only the name 'Saltmarsh Quay' in bold body text next to a stock anchor icon; no designed mark, no colour or type moment of the harbour's own on any screen.
Headings differ from body only in size and weight; one sans family throughout, no typographic moment.

Half-empty right side at wide widths: content column stops at ~750px inside a 1072px container on every route, leaving the right third empty (berths/default/1280, boat/default/1280, review/default/1280).
Footer band stops short on short pages: white footer followed by an empty grey field below (boat/default/1280, review/default/1280, confirmed/default/1280, length-over-limit/1440).
Sections that are only a heading and a list: 'Harbour rules' on root.
Orphaned kebab '...' button floating at the far right above the berth list with an empty band beside it (berths/default/1280).
Stranded fragment: 'Reference BK-' / '409.' broken across lines (length-over-limit/375).
evidence: First viewport on every route is a heading, a sentence and a stack of default form fields on a flat pale ground; nothing rewards a look (root/default/1280, boat/default/1280).
The tide table, the one element of the harbour's own, is a default table with misaligned headers (left-aligned 'Morning'/'Afternoon' over right-aligned times) and stops at 688px (root/default/1280).
Confirmation page is a heading, three label/value rows and a link above a mostly empty viewport (confirmed/default/1280).
Clean and orderly at every width, nothing broken or clashing, so not 'unappealing'; but it reads as a default form.
